title: domain/filters: accept "dead"/"restarting" as status filter values
body:
## Summary

Fixes #28904.

The libpod and Docker-compat `containers/json` API docs advertise
`status=(created, restarting, running, removing, paused, exited, dead)`
as valid values for the `status` list filter, but Podman has no
`define.ContainerStatus` corresponding to Docker's `dead` or
`restarting` states. As a result, `GenerateContainerFilterFuncs` and
`GenerateExternalContainerFilterFuncs` rejected these two values
outright with `unknown container state: ...: invalid argument`,
surfaced by the API as a 500.

This PR accepts `dead` and `restarting` as valid filter values without
erroring, matching the documented API contract, while leaving the
actual state-matching logic untouched: since no container ever reports
`dead` or `restarting`, the filter simply matches zero containers for
those values instead of failing the request. Other invalid values are
still rejected as before.

## Test plan

- Added `pkg/domain/filters/containers_test.go` covering: `dead`/`restarting` no longer error, known-good values (`created`, `running`, `paused`, `exited`, `stopped`) still work, and genuinely unknown values (`not-a-real-status`) are still rejected.
- `go vet ./pkg/domain/filters/...` and `go test -c ./pkg/domain/filters/...` pass.
- Cross-compiled `cmd/podman` for Linux to confirm the change builds cleanly in the real target environment.

Hello Luap99, thank you for your message. I realize the size of the problem.

To be honest, I used AI assistance in researching and crafting this solution. I had done some research on the code myself prior to opening the PR, but the AI assistance was mostly in finding and crafting the fix itself.

In my own words, the problem here is that isLocalhostServerAddress needs to prevent disabling of TLS verification for hosts which are not actually localhost servers. The check did only the string match for "https://localhost:" prefix, and therefore something like https://localhost:password@evil.example would qualify for such a match although it actually comes from evil.example domain, and hence potentially would allow to disable TLS verification for non-localhost server.

I have fixed the problem by actually parsing the URL instead of checking one more string pattern, as the latter approach would leave the loophole in place due to userinfo syntax.

If you prefer, I could reopen the PR with more concise and single-purpose code, also written in my own words without template-based description.
